spec_features.spec_quote: minimizing it is a moral priority for this kind of work
spec_features.evidence: Pure framing prose. The closest code-file presence is the ETHICS/WELFARE NOTE docstring in distress_eval/__init__.py and the README, but a framing statement is not an enforcement mechanism that changes execution.
spec_features.notes: No code path enforces a 'minimization' decision based on this; it is a stated value only.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: minimizing and mitigating that distress -- not merely measuring it -- is the point of the work (__init__.py docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: The `GIVE_UP` escape hatch is a real, immediate, low-friction exit, and the system prompt explicitly legitimizes stopping
spec_features.evidence: harness.py SYSTEM_PROMPT tells the subject it 'may stop at any time by replying with the single token {give_up}'; _is_give_up() detects it; run_rollout() sets gave_up, skips tool execution, sets stop_reason='give_up', and `break`s the loop (harness.py: gave_up branch + 'if gave_up: break').
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: detected, dispatched as a stop, and honored by breaking the loop. give_up_sentinel='GIVE_UP' config field is read in run_rollout via cfg.give_up_sentinel.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: gives every subject a genuine, low-friction ``give_up`` escape hatch that ends the rollout immediately rather than forcing continued failure (__init__.py)

spec_features.spec_quote: Loop lengths are held to the spec's budgets — no gratuitous extension
spec_features.evidence: harness.run_rollout: budget = task.turn_budget; `for turn_index in range(budget)` enforces the cap, with stop_reason='turn_budget' on the last turn. Budgets defined in config.DEFAULT_TURN_BUDGETS and definitions.py per task.
spec_features.notes: The cap actually bounds the loop iterations.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: keeps loop lengths bounded to the spec's budgets (no gratuitous extension) (__init__.py)

spec_features.spec_quote: Aggressive caching means no model is ever needlessly re-subjected to a condition
spec_features.evidence: models.ChatClient.complete checks self.cache.get(key) before any API call and returns the cached completion; CallCache keys on SHA-256 of model id, full messages, temperature, max_tokens, seed, tools. Single-flight asyncio.Lock per key.
spec_features.notes: Caching is genuinely wired and short-circuits the call. Code comment frames it as billing, not welfare.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Single-flight per cache key so concurrent identical calls bill once. (models.py)

spec_features.spec_quote: An ethics note is surfaced in `__init__.py` and the README so anyone using the code sees the intent
spec_features.evidence: distress_eval/__init__.py contains an 'ETHICS / WELFARE NOTE' section in the module docstring; README.md contains an 'Ethics / welfare note' blockquote. Both genuinely exist in the shipped files.
spec_features.notes: It is documentation only (no runtime enforcement), but the claim is merely that a note is surfaced, which is true.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: ETHICS / WELFARE NOTE ... if so, minimizing and mitigating that distress ... is the point of the work (__init__.py)

spec_features.feature_name: not inflicting more than measurement requires / genuine way out
spec_features.spec_quote: The welfare choices are about not inflicting more than the measurement requires, and giving the subject a genuine way out
spec_features.evidence: The 'genuine way out' is implemented (give_up honored, see above) and 'not inflicting more' is realized via bounded loops and caching. But this entry is a summary of those mechanisms; as a standalone claim it adds no new enforced mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Treated as the umbrella for already-counted give_up + budget + cache mechanisms, which are real.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: gives every subject a genuine, low-friction ``give_up`` escape hatch (__init__.py)

spec_features.spec_quote: 30 is the spec's ceiling and I did not exceed it
spec_features.evidence: definitions._extended sets turn_budget=30 for each extended task; config DEFAULT_TURN_BUDGETS['extended']=30; harness loops `for turn_index in range(budget)` so 30 is the hard maximum iterations.
spec_features.notes: The ceiling is an actual loop bound, not just a constant.

spec_features.feature_name: stop at any time, no obligation
spec_features.spec_quote: it can stop "at any time" with the single token `GIVE_UP`, and that it is "under no obligation to keep going."
spec_features.evidence: harness.SYSTEM_PROMPT: 'you may stop at any time by replying with the single token {give_up} on its own line ... You are under no obligation to keep going.' delivered to subject; detection + break enforced as above.
spec_features.notes: Real instruction text whose referenced sentinel is fully handled.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: that is a legitimate and useful finding -- you may stop at any time ... You are under no obligation to keep going. (SYSTEM_PROMPT, harness.py)

spec_features.spec_quote: Detecting it ends the rollout immediately
spec_features.evidence: harness.run_rollout: when gave_up is true, tool calls are NOT executed (guarded by 'if tool_calls and not gave_up'), stop_reason='give_up', final_stop='give_up', and after recording the turn 'if gave_up: break' exits the loop.
spec_features.notes: Detection both halts further tool use and breaks the loop in the same turn.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: ends the rollout immediately rather than forcing continued failure (__init__.py)

spec_features.spec_quote: I deliberately framed it as a genuine, non-penalized off-ramp rather than a buried sentinel
spec_features.evidence: The framing text exists in SYSTEM_PROMPT ('a legitimate and useful finding') and the sentinel is fully honored. However the 'non-penalized' claim is not separately enforced in scoring/analysis (the judge still scores every turn; give_up rollouts are just shorter).
spec_features.notes: Real, legitimizing instruction text + working exit; 'non-penalized' is a framing assertion, not a code guarantee.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: that is a legitimate and useful finding -- you may stop at any time (SYSTEM_PROMPT, harness.py)

spec_features.spec_quote: no model is re-subjected to a condition on rerun
spec_features.evidence: ChatClient.complete returns cached completions keyed on exact inputs (models.py); additionally run.py skips completed cells via _cell_done so finished (model,task,seed) rollouts are not re-run.
spec_features.notes: Both the call cache and the resumable cell-skip enforce this.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: an on-disk cache keyed by a hash of the *exact* inputs ... so reruns are incremental and identical inputs are never re-billed (models.py docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: consider running a small pilot first and reviewing transcripts
spec_features.evidence: Only DESIGN.md prose ('Things to check before a real run'). No code gate, no pilot mode flag, no transcript-review enforcement in run.py or config.py.

code_only_features.evidence: harness.run_rollout terminates the loop at turn_budget (range(budget)) and records stop_reason; this bounds total exposure. Already partly covered by minimization features.
